old: In 1808 John Dalton proposed his atomic theory, which has five postulates. First, matter consists of indivisible atoms. Second, all atoms of an element are identical in mass and properties, while atoms of different elements differ. Third, compounds form when atoms of different elements combine in a fixed ratio. Fourth, chemical reactions only rearrange atoms; atoms are neither created nor destroyed. Fifth, the theory explains the laws of conservation of mass, definite proportions and multiple proportions. Key terms follow from this picture. An atom is the smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction. A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and has all its properties. An element contains only one kind of atom, for example $Na$, $H_2$, $O_3$ or $S_8$. A compound contains two or more kinds of atoms in a fixed ratio, for example $H_2O$ or $CO_2$. The theory has limitations. It cannot explain the law of gaseous volumes. Discoveries of subatomic particles, isotopes and isobars showed that atoms are divisible and that atoms of one element can differ in mass.
new: In 1808 John Dalton proposed his atomic theory, which has four main postulates. First, matter consists of indivisible atoms. Second, all atoms of an element are identical in mass and properties, while atoms of different elements differ. Third, compounds form when atoms of different elements combine in a fixed ratio. Fourth, chemical reactions only rearrange atoms; atoms are neither created nor destroyed. The theory was able to explain the laws of conservation of mass, definite proportions and multiple proportions. Key terms follow from this picture. An atom is the smallest particle of an element that can take part in a chemical reaction. A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and has all its properties. An element contains only one kind of atom, for example $Na$, $H_2$, $O_3$ or $S_8$. A compound contains two or more kinds of atoms in a fixed ratio, for example $H_2O$ or $CO_2$. The theory has limitations. It cannot explain the law of gaseous volumes. Discoveries of subatomic particles showed that atoms are divisible. Isotopes showed that atoms of one element can differ in mass, and isobars showed that atoms of different elements can have the same mass.
fixes: Four postulates, not five (explaining the laws is a success, not a postulate); isobars show that atoms of different elements can have the same mass, while isotopes show that atoms of one element can differ in mass
